chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill. He said: She inherits him during his illness for the period between him and one year, if he dies in that illness. And she observes the waiting period of the divorced woman from the day he divorced her. Then she may marry if she wishes after her waiting period ends, and she inherits him between her and one year, if he dies in that illness. But if he dies after the year passes, she has no inheritance. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains from his saying 'then she may marry if she wishes after her waiting period ends, and she inherits him between her and one year' does not contradict what we have presented that when she marries, she does not inherit him, because most of what is in this report is the explicit permission for her to marry after the end of the waiting period. And his saying 'and she inherits him between her and one year' is a ruling specific to her if she does not marry, indicated by what we have presented from the reports that what I choose is that she only inherits him after the end of the waiting period if he divorced her for her detriment. And all the general reports that preceded are to be understood according to this distinction, indicating that.

key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a wife if her husband divorces her while he is ill?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar establishes the 'marad al-mawt' (death illness) period as one year for inheritance purposes when a husband divorces his wife while ill, a ruling derived from the principle that such divorce is often deemed 'for detriment' (li-l-dharar). Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the scholarly nuance that remarriage does not automatically negate her inheritance right, interpreting the text to mean she retains the share unless she remarries, thereby reconciling seemingly contradictory reports through the lens of the divorce's intent.
